name: Deep-Sea & Open-Ocean Ecosystems
genZNote: We've mapped more of the Moon's surface in detail than we have of the deep ocean floor — most of this ecosystem is still genuinely unexplored.

sections.heading: 🌊 The Open Ocean (Pelagic Zone)
bullets: The vast water column away from coastlines and the seafloor, divided into zones by depth and light penetration (sunlit surface layer, twilight zone, and the permanently dark deep zone).
Most open-ocean life depends, directly or indirectly, on phytoplankton — microscopic, photosynthesizing organisms that form the base of the entire marine food web.
Plankton also produce a very large share of the world's oxygen through photosynthesis, making them globally significant beyond just feeding fish.

sections.heading: 🔬 The Deep Sea
bullets: Below the reach of sunlight, deep-sea life depends on food sinking down from above, or in a few remarkable cases, chemosynthesis — bacteria producing energy from chemicals rather than light, found around hydrothermal vents.
Hydrothermal vents host entire ecosystems (tube worms, unique crustaceans) that don't depend on sunlight at all — one of the most significant discoveries in marine biology.
Extreme pressure, cold, and darkness make the deep sea one of the least explored environments on Earth, despite covering most of the planet's surface.

sections.heading: 🐟 Food Webs & Fisheries
bullets: Marine food webs generally run: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → larger predatory fish/marine mammals, with energy lost at each step.
Major global fisheries (tuna, sardines, anchovies) depend on productive open-ocean zones, often linked to nutrient upwelling near coastlines.
Overfishing pressure on open-ocean predator species (like tuna and sharks) is a widely tracked global conservation concern.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Open-ocean and deep-sea ecosystems range from sunlit surface waters powered by phytoplankton to permanently dark deep zones, some powered by chemosynthesis at hydrothermal vents.
keyFacts: Phytoplankton form the base of the open-ocean food web and produce much of the world's oxygen.
Deep sea = below sunlight penetration; depends on sinking food or chemosynthesis.
Hydrothermal vents host ecosystems independent of sunlight.
Food web: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → larger predators.
commonConfusion: Chemosynthesis (chemical-energy-based, found at vents) is distinct from photosynthesis (light-based, found near the surface) — don't conflate them.

highYieldFacts: Phytoplankton = base of the marine food web; major global oxygen producer.
Hydrothermal vent ecosystems run on chemosynthesis, not photosynthesis.
Deep sea remains one of Earth's least-explored environments.
commonTraps: Don't assume all deep-sea life depends on surface sunlight indirectly — vent ecosystems are a genuine exception.
mustRemember: Open ocean = phytoplankton-powered food web; deep sea = sinking food + rare chemosynthesis at vents.
